source.title: Derry Journal, 6 October 1937, p. 5 ("Derry municipal elections: yesterday's nominations; no contests in any ward")
source.publisher: Derry Journal (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: deemed re-elected: no nomination for the West Ward; 'Nationalists had made no nominations ... Councillors Andrew M'Closkey and William Quigley are the retiring Nationalist councillors in the West Ward, and Councillors B. Doherty and Frank Callaghan in the South. It is thought these may be automatically returned' (Derry Journal 6 Oct 1937 p5). Under the county borough election order (S.R.&O. 1929 No. 135, r.10(5)) the retiring councillors were declared deemed re-elected; confirmed on the cited page (round-2 final, 7 Nov 2026): the Nationalists 'had made no nominations', the Unionists were nominated only 'in the remaining three Wards' (North, East and Waterside), and the only other nomination was Mr. Michael M'Nutt's, 'to fill the extra vacancy created in the South Ward', so no one was nominated for the West Ward's two seats.

note: Annual retirement of two councillors in each of the five wards of Londonderry Corporation, held in October after the ordinary day was moved for 1937; nominations Tuesday 5 October 1937. The Nationalists made no nominations, holding the election pointless with the whole Corporation due to retire in May 1938 under the new wards scheme; their retiring South and West councillors (B. Doherty and Frank Callaghan; Andrew M'Closkey and William Quigley) were deemed re-elected with no nomination, which the round-2 gap-fill (7 Nov 2026) records as the election it was; Michael M'Nutt was nominated, unopposed, for an extra South Ward vacancy. The Unionist nominees in North, East and Waterside were returned unopposed and there was no poll (Derry Journal, 6 October 1937). No nominations were made for the West Ward; its two retiring councillors were deemed re-elected (round-2 gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
